description: Full = capture all guest memory; Diff = capture only pages dirtied since last snapshot. Diff requires track_dirty_pages=true on the original boot.
Output path for the VM-state metadata file. Contains KVM state, device state, vCPU registers, MSRs, CPUID, and a 64-bit CRC of the file contents.
Output path for the guest memory file. Size = guest RAM for Full; smaller for Diff. Must remain on host for the lifetime of resumed microVMs that point at it.
Optional snapshot format version — emit an older format for backward compatibility with older Firecracker readers.
Path to the VM-state file to restore from. Firecracker validates the embedded CRC before proceeding.
File = MAP_PRIVATE the memory file (fast restore, file pinned for VM lifetime). Uffd = userfaultfd-driven on-demand load (orchestrator-supplied page handler).
For File backend: path to the memory file. For Uffd backend: path to a Unix socket where Firecracker sends the userfaultfd file descriptor to the handler process.
After restore, re-enable KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES so the resumed microVM can produce further diff snapshots. Required if you plan to take diff snapshots from the restored VM.
When true, automatically transition VM to Resumed after restore. When false (default), VM stays Paused — call PATCH /vm{state=Resumed} when ready.
Sets KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES on the guest RAM region. REQUIRED for taking diff snapshots later. Slight per-write overhead from KVM dirty-bit page-walk.
Snapshots restore much faster on cgroups v2 hosts. v1 imposes a significant latency tax (firecracker-microvm/firecracker#2129). Production deployments must use v2.
Required on the RESTORE host if the original snapshot was taken on a host with a different TSC frequency. Without it, restore fails with a TSC mismatch error.
